props.title: A Copy of the Screen

B01.capture_spec: C01: scene_c01_pool.gd (evidence/planning-checks), canvas 1280 x 720 through the 4K SubViewport route, 30 fps, Forward+, length = the beat's audio. Nothing moves but the water (TIME). Same capture serves B28.
B01.visual_intent: Act title 'A Copy of the Screen' (serif 40) top-left. A real Godot render in a framed window on the cream stage: a meadow of green checker tiles, a sand path, flowers, and in the lower left a pool whose wavy top edge ripples and whose water bends the checker lines and the path behind it. The teal player stands to the right. A terracotta ring settles on the pool.
B01.motion_claim: The water ripples and the checker lines behind it wobble, live; the ring marks where the picture behind is being read.

show.event: meadow with the live pool; act title top-left
terracotta ring settles on the pool

B01.runner_up: manim drawing of a glass pane over a scene
B01.why: The finished effect running is the question the film answers; a drawing would only claim it.

B02.visual_intent: On the cream stage a 16:9 screen frame, left, fills in the order the game draws it: the green checker ground, a tree, a flower, then a small rectangle labelled 'shader'. Just before that rectangle is drawn, a camera-flash snapshot copies the whole frame into a second frame on the right, labelled 'screen texture: a copy of everything drawn so far'. A drawn arrow runs from the shader rectangle to the copy.
B02.motion_claim: The frame is copied in one flash and the shader's arrow reads from the copy, not from the live frame.

show.event: screen frame; ground, tree, flower drawn in order
flash: the frame is copied to the right
arrow from the shader rectangle to the copy

B02.why: A snapshot being taken is a motion, and the arrow into the copy is the claim; an isometric flow would show boxes, not a copy of a picture.

cues.label: fragment(): runs once for each pixel

props.videoLabel: Godot 4.7.2 · Forward+ · shader switched on mid-clip (58 percent)

B03.capture_spec: C02: scene_c02_window.gd, 1280 x 720 canvas through the 4K SubViewport route, 30 fps, Forward+, length = the beat's audio. A teal rectangle (0.38, 0.22, 0.30 x 0.30 of the canvas) in a cream frame; 01-window is assigned at u = 0.58. Verified: the rectangle's interior equals the meadow exactly (8,820 samples, worst channel difference 0).
B03.visual_intent: Code card at left with the 7-line shader; at right a real Godot window on the meadow: a plain teal rectangle in a cream frame. At 58 percent the shader switches on and the teal fill vanishes, leaving the cream frame around meadow. Label: 'still there'.
B03.motion_claim: The teal rectangle vanishes at the cue; the cream frame stays, empty, showing the meadow.

show.event: the shader switches on; the teal fill vanishes

B03.why: Code and its result side by side, with the vanishing as the proof; code alone cannot show that the rectangle is still there.

B04.visual_intent: The line `uniform sampler2D screen_texture : hint_screen_texture;` set in monospace on the cream stage, each token its own object at explicit coordinates. A bracket is drawn under `uniform` with the label 'from outside'; one under `sampler2D` with 'sampler2D: the type of a texture a shader reads'; one under `screen_texture` with 'your name'. The `hint_screen_texture` token stays grey until the next beat.
B04.motion_claim: Each bracket is drawn under its token on the word that names it, so the line is read left to right.
B04.why: The pieces of one line need brackets under tokens; ShaderLab highlights whole lines only.

B05.visual_intent: The same line again with the `hint_screen_texture` token ringed (terracotta ring, grey backing) and the labels 'hint: the word after a colon that tells Godot how to treat a uniform' and 'this one: fill it with the screen'. Below, a slot labelled `screen_texture`. On three frame ticks (a small counter 1, 2, 3) a fresh miniature of the meadow drops into the slot, replacing the last one; in each the flower has moved a little. A small cursor arrow outside the slot is crossed out: 'you never set it'.
B05.motion_claim: A new copy drops into the slot on every tick, replacing the old one, with nobody placing it.

show.event: first copy drops into the slot

B05.why: Replacement on every tick is the claim 'Godot refreshes it every frame'; a static diagram could not show that the copy changes.

B06.visual_intent: The screen texture drawn as a 12 by 7 grid of outline cells in the meadow colours (cells are never filled behind text). A terracotta probe ring sits on one cell with a live label 'address (0.62, 0.40)'; a drawn arrow runs to a swatch showing that cell's colour. The probe hops to two more cells and the swatch follows. After the third hop the swatch splits into four chips R, G, B, A; the A chip carries 'alpha: how visible a pixel is (0 invisible, 1 solid)'.
B06.motion_claim: The probe hops from cell to cell and the swatch changes colour to match; then the swatch splits into four numbers.

show.event: swatch splits into R, G, B, A

B06.why: An address going in and a color coming out is a lookup, and a lookup is a probe on a grid; code would only name it.

B07.visual_intent: A 16:9 screen outline with a smaller 4:3 shape inside it and one pixel dot on the shape. Two live labels follow the dot: 'UV (0.5, 0.5)', measured on the shape ('UV: a point's address on the shape'), and 'screen UV (0.31, 0.62)', measured on the screen ('SCREEN_UV: a pixel's address on the whole screen, not on its own shape'). The shape then slides right: the first label stays (0.5, 0.5) while the second counts up to (0.62, 0.62).
B07.motion_claim: The shape slides and one label never changes while the other counts up.

show.event: the shape slides; screen UV counts up

B07.runner_up: ShaderLab with the two colour pictures
B07.why: Two numbers changing at different rates is exactly a pair of live labels; the real render comes in the next beat.

B08.capture_spec: C03: scene_c03_addresses.gd, 1280 x 720 canvas through the 4K SubViewport route, 30 fps, Forward+, length = the beat's audio. Top rectangle 02-miniature, bottom 01-window, both 0.28 x 0.28, sliding from x = 0.04 to 0.56 between u = 0.15 and 0.90. Verified: inside the miniature the colour at a fraction of the rectangle equals the screen at the same fraction (4 of 4 points); inside the window it equals the screen at the same place.
B08.visual_intent: Two 16:9 rectangles in cream frames, one above the other, slide right together over the meadow. The top one (UV) holds a tiny copy of the whole screen that does not move with the picture; the bottom one (screen UV) is a window onto the meadow. Right-margin labels 'UV' and 'screen UV'.
B08.motion_claim: Both rectangles slide; the top one keeps showing the same tiny copy, the bottom one shows different parts of the meadow.

show.event: label 'screen UV' by the bottom rectangle

B08.runner_up: manim drawing of the two cases
B08.why: The consequence of the wrong address is a tiny copy of the screen inside a rectangle, and that is only convincing as a real render.

cues.label: .rgb: picks red, green and blue (a swizzle)

B09.capture_spec: C04: scene_c04_invert.gd, 1280 x 720 canvas through the 4K SubViewport route, 30 fps, Forward+, length = the beat's audio. 03-invert in a 0.28 x 0.28 window that is still until u = 0.56, then slides from (0.08, 0.10) to (0.62, 0.58) by u = 0.96. Verified: every sampled pixel equals 1 minus the meadow (worst channel difference 0).
B09.visual_intent: Code card at left (the 8-line invert shader); at right a real Godot window: one 16:9 window in a cream frame holds the meadow with every colour flipped (greens turn purple, the sand path turns navy). It sits still, then slides diagonally across the meadow; the flipped picture inside stays pinned to the screen while the opening moves. Label 'pinned to screen'.
B09.motion_claim: The window slides and the flipped picture inside does not slide with it; only the opening moves.
B09.runner_up: manim sliding frame over a picture
B09.why: The sliding window over a fixed picture is the claim, shown on the real result next to the one line that flips it.

props.title: A line from older tutorials
props.note: Godot 4.7.2 compiler: SCREEN_TEXTURE has been removed in favor of using hint_screen_texture with a uniform.

B10.visual_intent: A cream code card with the five-line shader that uses the capital-letters shortcut; focus lands on the line that uses it. Under the card the engine's own message, verbatim from a real run, is the note.
B10.motion_claim: Focus steps down to the old line and stays on it while the compiler's message is read.

show.event: focus on the shader's first lines
settled: old line and the compiler's message

B10.runner_up: BrowserCapture of the docs row 'SCREEN_TEXTURE: Removed in Godot 4'
B10.why: The real message from a real run is the thing a viewer will actually see; the docs row says the same but is not what appears when it fails.
